Groom to Bride: So much better than wine are your breasts,
fragranced with the finest perfumes. Bride to Groom:
Your name is oil that has been poured out;
therefore, the maidens have loved you.
post te curremus in odorem unguentorum tuorum.
Chorus to Bride: We will run after you in the odor of your perfumes.
Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua;
Bride to Chorus: The king has led me into his storerooms.
Chorus to Bride: We will exult and rejoice in you,
remembering your breasts above wine. Groom to Bride:
Nolite me considerare quod fusca sim,
Do not be concerned that I am dark,
for the sun has changed my color.
Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me;
The sons of my mother have fought against me.
They have made me the keeper of the vineyards.
My own vineyard I have not kept.
Reveal to me, you whom my soul loves,
ne vagari incipiam post greges sodalium tuorum.
lest I begin to wander after the flocks of your companions.
If you yourself do not know,
then go out and follow after the steps of the flocks,
et pasce hædos tuos juxta tabernacula pastorum.
and pasture your young goats beside the tabernacles of the shepherds.
Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te,
I have compared you to my company of horsemen against the chariots of Pharaoh.
Pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ sicut turturis;
Your cheeks are beautiful, like those of a turtledove.
Your neck is like a bejeweled collar.
Chorus to Bride: We will fashion for you chains of gold,
Dum esset rex in accubitu suo,
Bride to Chorus: While the king was taking his rest,
my aromatic ointment sent forth its odor.
My beloved is a bundle of myrrh to me.
He shall abide between my breasts.
Botrus cypri dilectus meus mihi in vineis Engaddi.
My beloved is a cluster of Cyprus grapes to me, in the vineyards of Engaddi.
O my love. Behold, you are beautiful.
Your eyes are those of a dove.
